title: Programmable proteases designed to cut any chosen site

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 8, Programmable proteases. Target: within 24 hours, design a protease that efficiently cleaves a blinded site in a folded protein in living cells; the full challenge is 20 preregistered sites at over 80% success; cleaving preregistered peptides in solution counts as partial success. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BCH on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Programmable proteases
page.definition: The goal is to choose an accessible peptide bond, the link between two adjacent amino acids in a folded protein that a cell naturally makes, and design a protease on demand that cuts that bond efficiently and selectively in living cells. Designed proteases can already cut selected sites in amyloid-β peptides in solution.

goal.need: During programmed cell death, enzymes called caspases cut more than 1,500 proteins. Mapping those cuts leaves open which ones cause a particular change in the cell. One way to isolate a cut requires replacing the target protein with a version that a known protease recognises. Choosing a site in the native protein would let cell biologists test what that cut alone does. Selective cleavage could also inactivate a disease-associated protein. Both uses depend on reaching the intended bond and sparing other proteins.

statements.body: Westlake University and Westlake Laboratory of Life Sciences and Biomedicine
statements.quote: An enduring objective is therefore to create “molecular scalpels” whose cleavage site can be programmed at will

completion.title: Protease designs pass more than 80% of a 20-site blinded cellular challenge.
completion.criterion: Produce designs within 24 hours of preregistration for 20 blinded, accessible sites in endogenous folded proteins. At least 17 sites must be cleaved efficiently in living cells. Compare each enzyme’s catalytic efficiency and proteome-wide off-target cleavage with those of widely used site-specific proteases. The protocol accepts similarity or a greater value for both measures and gives no separate scoring direction for off-target cleavage. After targets are supplied, the only laboratory work allowed before evaluation is production of the designed proteins for assay.
completion.basis: Problem 8's declared endpoint. Published design hit rates do not establish success across blinded targets.

milestones.title: A designed protease catalyses cleavage at its intended peptide bond in vitro.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate enzyme-dependent hydrolysis at the intended peptide bond in a chosen substrate in vitro and show catalytic turnover.
milestones.set_by: Protease-design research convention, exemplified by Chen et al. and Choi et al.; a qualitative catalytic-activity test without a shared numerical activity cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: catalyse cleavage of their cognate peptide substrates at the targeted scissile bond.

milestones.title: Designed proteases cleave preregistered peptides in solution while discriminating off-target sequences.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate efficient, selective cleavage of preregistered target peptide sequences supplied in solution together with off-target sequences.
milestones.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific; Problem 8, partial success.
milestones.threshold_quote: specifically and efficiently cleave specific preregistered peptide sequences

milestones.title: One blinded cellular target passes the challenge's 24-hour design test.
milestones.criterion: For one preregistered, blinded, accessible site in an endogenous folded protein, produce the design within 24 hours of preregistration. Demonstrate efficient cleavage at that site in living cells under the completion test’s catalytic-efficiency and proteome-wide off-target comparison. After target disclosure, limit laboratory work before evaluation to producing the designed protein for assay.
milestones.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific; Problem 8's per-site prerequisite.
milestones.threshold_quote: cleaves that site efficiently in living cells.

not_found: No public report of the 20-site blinded evaluation or the preregistered solution-phase partial-success test was located.
No comparator panel, numerical activity/off-target tolerances, or unambiguous off-target comparison direction is specified.
No numerical field-wide threshold for the initial laboratory demonstration was located in protease-design benchmarks, roadmaps or the cited papers.
No statement from a scientific society or challenge programme disputing the value or feasibility of Problem 8 was located.

results.finding: Of 135 designed metalloproteases, 36% cleaved their cognate peptide at the intended bond.
results.detail: Extended Data Fig. 7d reports a 5-hour total-turnover assay for Zn45_v2, repeated three times with similar results. The caption does not state the numerical turnover value.
results.quote: Of 135 designs tested, 36% catalyse cleavage of their cognate peptide substrates at the targeted scissile bond.

results.finding: Two designed metalloproteases were tested in triplicate on cognate and alternative substrates.
results.detail: The excerpt gives no numerical selectivity result for the two-design comparison.
results.quote: Reaction progress curves of SAAc8 and AbetaF3 on their cognate substrates, and on other substrates presented in this work. Measurements were made in triplicate.

results.finding: DP622-S2, one of five active designs, hydrolyzed its intended amyloid-β bond in vitro with a kcat of 0.00191 s⁻¹.
results.detail: The turnover rate came from an amyloid-β segment embedded in a FRET reporter. Mass spectrometry mapped the cleavage bond in a separate fusion-substrate assay.
results.quote:
Among  the  designed
proteases, DP622-S2 demonstrated the highest catalytic effi-
ciency, achieving a kcat/Km of 325.26 M−1s−1, driven by a favor-
able  combination  of  a  high kcat (0.00191 s−1)  and  a  low Km
(5.87  μM).

results.finding: OP609-S2 cleaved only its intended fusion substrate in a three-substrate panel and reached a catalytic efficiency of 3045.14 M⁻¹s⁻¹.
results.detail: Selectivity was measured with amyloid-β segments embedded in fusion proteins. The full-length synthetic Aβ42 assay established cleavage of the free peptide.
results.quote:

3045.14 M−1s−1 (Fig. 5c),

results.finding: De novo cysteine proteases showed cleavage activity in 13 of 69 designs screened.
results.detail: Extended Data Figs. 3–6 report site confirmation, catalytic-residue controls, intermolecular peptide cleavage and turnover assays. The excerpt gives theoretical maximum turnover numbers but omits the observed values.
results.quote: In all cases, the mass spectra confirmed cleavage at the designed site.

results.finding: Active designs cleaved cognate peptides at 200 µM substrate. The number of pairs assayed is unstated.
results.quote: FRET measurements for each design with its cognate FRET-paired peptide substrate. Reactions were performed with 10 µM enzyme and 200 µM substrate in a fluorescence plate reader.

results.finding: Dokki and its variants showed cleavage in a HeLa reporter assay with three independent experiments.
results.detail: The 24-hour interval measured time from transfection to imaging.
results.quote: The designed proteases efficiently cleave their targets in mammalian cells, opening the door to a wide range of synthetic biology applications.

results.finding: TTRg11 cleaved the intended bond in a transthyretin peptide reporter in vitro with a kcat of 0.072 ± 0.008 s⁻¹ (triplicate measurements).
results.detail: The chosen substrate was a transthyretin-derived peptide embedded between sfGFP and mScarlet.
results.quote: TTRg11 exhibited a kcat of 0.072 ± 0.008 s −1

definition = "The goal is to choose an accessible peptide bond, the link between two adjacent amino acids in a folded protein that a cell naturally makes, and design a protease on demand that cuts that bond efficiently and selectively in living cells. Designed proteases can already cut selected sites in amyloid-\u03b2 peptides in solution.". Reason: The present tense implies that on-demand cellular design is already possible and omits the restriction to accessible sites in native proteins.

goal.need = "During programmed cell death, enzymes called caspases cut more than 1,500 proteins. Mapping those cuts leaves open which ones cause a particular change in the cell. One way to isolate a cut requires replacing the target protein with a version that a known protease recognises. Choosing a site in the native protein would let cell biologists test what that cut alone does. Selective cleavage could also inactivate a disease-associated protein. Both uses depend on reaching the intended bond and sparing other proteins.". Reason: The existing paragraph recounts one evolution experiment but leaves out the biological question that control over a single cut would let people answer.

edit completion: criterion = "Produce designs within 24 hours of preregistration for 20 blinded, accessible sites in endogenous folded proteins. After targets are supplied, the only laboratory work allowed before evaluation is production of the designed proteins for assay."; threshold_quote = "similar to or greater than"; threshold_ref = 2. Reason: “Match or exceed” changes the protocol’s allowance for similarity and makes greater unintended cleavage sound like better performance.

edit m1: criterion = "Demonstrate enzyme-dependent hydrolysis at the intended peptide bond in a chosen substrate in vitro and show catalytic turnover.". Reason: The two reported design hit rates are results and do not define the test for cleavage of the intended bond.

edit m2: criterion = "Demonstrate efficient, selective cleavage of preregistered target peptide sequences supplied in solution together with off-target sequences.". Reason: The amyloid-β findings and the discussion of their preregistration status belong with the evidence for this milestone.
